name: Subset Teaching Dimension of Singletons
proof: For $n=1$, the only ordinary minimum sample is empty and the subset recursion stays at value zero. For $n\ge3$, each singleton has just its positive example as an ordinary minimum sample: a single negative example leaves $n-1\ge2$ concepts consistent. For $n=2$, each target has two minimum singleton samples, its own positive example and the negative example on the other coordinate. In both cases $n\ge2$, all these samples have size one and samples assigned to distinct targets are different. A singleton sample is contained in a previous singleton sample exactly when they are equal, so each remains uniquely owned by its target. The empty sample has every target as an owner. Hence the entire families of minimum samples remain fixed, with value one.
